title: The Pause Between Failure and Agreement
headline: How to Take Thoughts Captive After You Fail
headline_sub: The Pause Between Failure and Agreement
tagline: Not every thought is your own. But every thought becomes influential once you agree with it.
seo_title: Taking Thoughts Captive After Failure (2 Corinthians 10:5) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Not every thought deserves residence; some only deserve interrogation. A devotional for men on 2 Corinthians 10:5 and Philippians 4:8.
verse_text: Take every thought captive to obey Christ.

scriptures.text: Take every thought captive to obey Christ.
Whatever is true, noble, right, pure…. think about such things.

items: Inside that pause, two voices begin speaking.
Paul tells us to take every thought captive.
Because not every thought deserves residence.

blocks.text: Who benefits if I agree with this?
If agreement makes Christ appear farther away…. question the thought.

items: Paul doesn’t only tell us what to reject.
He also tells us what deserves our attention.
The battle isn’t only over your behavior.
It’s over what continually occupies your mind.
Whatever repeatedly holds your attention…. eventually shapes your life.
Not every thought is your own.
But every thought becomes influential once you agree with it.
